standard_prerequisites.name: Homogeneous generators for a finitely generated graded module
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the first line of the counted proof (lines 14097-14099)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the generating set to homogeneous elements by taking homogeneous components.

standard_prerequisites.name: Graded generation of the algebra over its degree-zero part
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the homogeneous generators f_i of S over S_0, which can be taken in positive degrees.

core_obligations: Choose generators of M and of S over S_0 and replace them by their homogeneous components, so that the generators m_i and f_i are homogeneous and the f_i lie in positive degrees (proof lines 14097-14100).

Write an arbitrary element of M_n as an S_0-linear combination of the monomials in the f_i times the m_j having total degree n, which exhibits M_n as finitely generated over S_0 (proof lines 14100-14103).
proof_roadmap: Make the chosen generators homogeneous and push the algebra generators into positive degrees (proof lines 14096-14100).
Generate each graded piece by the finitely many monomials of the correct degree (proof lines 14100-14104).
difficulty_reason: If M is a finitely generated graded module over a graded ring S which is finitely generated over S_0, the lemma states that each graded piece M_n is a finite S_0-module (statement lines 14089-14094). The proof does not use Hilbert functions or a Noetherian hypothesis: it replaces the generators by their homogeneous components, arranges the algebra generators in positive degrees, and then exhibits each M_n as generated over S_0 by the finitely many monomials of degree n in the algebra generators times the module generators (proof lines 14096-14104). The reduction to homogeneous generators is what makes the graded bookkeeping possible, and the author writes it out. H2.
